summary: The skill entity page covers CanonicalSkill: instructions the model gets only when they matter, with a name, a one-line description the model reads when it may pick the skill, and macro-rendered text. A skill turns on always, when its triggers match, or while the model has it open, and its triggers are a lorebook entry's own fields matched by the lore engine's own matcher. A scene links skills by id in its prompting like tools and trackers, a turn reads them through its one library reader, and the ones on ride as one Skills block at the preset's skills marker, reserved by the budget so they are never dropped. The model opens and closes picked skills with open_skill and close_skill, kept in the skills scene-state slot. The Workbench editor supports activation and trigger editing. Promptbook cards provide named placements and Together groups with fixed budget protection; the scene panel and Kit editing remain unbuilt. Live verification remains unavailable.

sections.title: When it is on
sections.summary: A skill's when is always, mentioned or picked. Always puts it in the prompt every turn while linked. Mentioned uses a lorebook entry's own trigger fields, decoded by the lorebook's trigger decoder and matched by the lore engine's matchTrigger and selectiveLogicMatches over the newest scanDepth messages, the one being answered included, newest first, with regex triggers vetted; no triggers or a scan depth of 0 never match, and a trigger's frequency and probability are kept but unused. Picked is on while the model has it open, and with closeWhenUnmentioned it closes when its triggers stop matching, unless it has no triggers or a scan depth of 0. Each verdict carries a plain sentence of why, returned on the assembly result.

sections.title: Open and closed
sections.summary: Which skills are open is scene state: the fields slot skills, one field per skill id holding true while open, written by the turn and the person, so a swipe, regenerate, cut or fork shows the open set of what is shown. A scene linking picked skills gives the model open_skill and close_skill while Narrator Tool Access is on. open_skill lists every picked skill's name and purpose in its description, answers with the skill's instructions rendered read-only with unanswered macros stripped, and opens it once through the turn's tool door. close_skill closes an open one and says so of one that is not. Both are stateScoped writes at tier narrator.skill; an unknown name is refused with the list. A close rule that holds is closed by the turn itself.

sections.title: In a scene and in the prompt
sections.summary: A scene links skills by id in ChatPrompting.skills, in order with no duplicates, by the same rule as tools and trackers. A turn reads them through its one library reader, leaving out gone, unreadable and same-named skills. The skills that are on ride as one system message headed Skills, each name a heading over its rendered text, in the scene's order, and a blank one adds nothing. The block goes where the preset's skills marker stands with that block's role, otherwise after the leading system messages after the trackers' and storyboards' blocks. The budget reserves it like the library trackers' block, so history gives way and it is never dropped. The Tokens sheet labels it Skills.

sections.title: Editing and placement
sections.summary: The Workbench editor uses the existing revision-checked piece session for instructions, activation and shared triggers. Primary matches can require any or all, with older pieces defaulting to any. Promptbook Skill cards occupy named positions and can join adjacent Prompt cards in one message, retaining existing activation and fixed budget protection. Duplicate named-slot placement through include is refused. The dedicated scene Skills panel, manual close route and Kit authoring remain unbuilt; generic Kit piece operations work. Editor and placement evidence is unit based, with live UI verification blocked by browser access.
